THE_FINDING_OF_THIS_SESSION: THE MEAN-PLUS-MARGIN RULE IS WRONG BY FIVE ORDERS OF MAGNITUDE AND IT IS WORST WHERE IT LOOKS SAFEST. On the 600 s ground-truth run at contention level 4, a margin of k = 5.221001 standard deviations to the deadline predicts P(response > D) = 8.897912e-08 against a counted 1.359977e-02 (816 misses in 60001 releases): UNDERSTATEMENT FACTOR 1.528423e+05, 95 per cent moving-block interval [3.635383e+04, 9.160321e+05], EXCLUDING 1. Across the ten mixes the pattern is the point: at mix_c2 a 20.261-sigma margin predicts 1.411300e-91 against a counted 1.333244e-04, while at mix_c5 and mix_c6, where the margin is under 1.4 sigma, the rule is within a factor of 1.53. The Gaussian rule is not useless; it is useless in the regime anyone would ship. The EVT fit on the same data gives 6.727478e-03, low by 2.0215 - competitive, and still reported as OUTSIDE the counted rate's interval, because being much better than the thing being refuted is not the same as being right.

THREE_CAMPAIGNS_RAN_AND_TWO_WERE_DISCARD: CAMPAIGN 1 (board 23:14:39, ran 36 minutes to completion, DISCARDED). All ten job traces written and valid; NOT ONE MONITOR FILE. The 1 Hz monitor is a subprocess of the campaign script and the launch omitted the --out argument that the script's own argparse declares required, so every monitor exited 2 before writing a row, with stderr sent to DEVNULL, while the campaign reported success. That defect alone would have removed every contention descriptor and with it the entire learned half of the product. Campaign 1 ALSO mis-sized the payload: it calibrated to 0.4499 of the deadline from a 1.2 s probe taken immediately after the board went idle, when schedutil had begun dropping the clock, and the sustained median across its runs then came out near 0.19 - a factor of 2.3 - leaving six of ten runs with ZERO misses and a miss-rate curve that was not monotone (0.0015 at four stressors, 0.0345 at five, 0.0005 at six). CAMPAIGN 2 (02:59:19, killed after 3 minutes) carried the same calibration and was killed; killing it LEFT FIVE ORPHANED CPU STRESSORS AT ~97 PER CENT EACH, found by listing the board's processes and killed by PID before campaign 3. A campaign launched on top of them would have measured five uncontrolled busy threads and called it a contention level. CAMPAIGN 3 (03:02:08, 37 minutes) is published. THE GENERAL LESSON: a campaign that completes is not a campaign that measured - both defects produced a clean exit status, a full log and a plausible set of files.

A_DESCRIPTOR_THE_SPECIFICATION_DOES_NOT_: The specification requires descriptors an operator could observe WITHOUT running the task. The measured feature importances put task_pct - the task's own CPU occupancy - first at 0.654312, and load1 includes the task in its run queue. The coordinator did not withdraw or retune the headline; it added validation/validate_descriptor_leak.py, which refits the same forest with the same seed and the same splits on two narrower sets. Removing task_pct costs 1.1813x grouped and 1.2714x on time; removing task_pct and load1 costs 1.1354x and 1.2619x, giving grouped MAE 0.028411 and time MAE 0.009249. The restricted figure STILL beats speed scaling at 0.043799 and the constant rate at 0.071455, so the conclusion survives the restriction and the full-set figure is published as an upper bound and labelled as one.
WEAK_RESULTS_PUBLISHED_RATHER_THAN_HIDDE: (1) THE PRE-REGISTERED EXPECTATION IN SPEC.md WAS REFUTED: it said the classical predictor would be competitive on the forecasting task and that any learned margin would be smaller than the counted reference's bootstrap interval; the forest won both splits by 13.3 and 23.8 half-widths. Published as refuted, with the mechanism named. (2) Speed scaling nevertheless WINS 5 OF THE 10 HELD-OUT RUNS - mix_c0, mix_c1, mix_c2, mix_c2mem1, mix_mem2 - every one a low-contention run; the forest wins the aggregate because the aggregate is dominated by the high-rate runs. (3) The forest's grouped bias is -0.015675, so on an unseen mix it UNDER-predicts risk, the dangerous direction. (4) Its worst held-out run is mix_c6 at MAE 0.227703 against a true 0.382601 - the extreme of the training range. (5) The EVT fit is OUTSIDE the counted rate's interval, low by 2.0215, and is reported as outside rather than as correct. (6) The GPD modified scale is NOT constant across candidate thresholds (-4.06 to -0.52), which says the asymptotic regime is not reached at the lower thresholds and is the honest reason the EVT probability is low. (7) mix_mem2 recorded ZERO misses in 15001 releases: two memory-bandwidth stressors produced no measurable deadline risk for this payload, and its understatement factor is exactly zero rather than a small number. (8) The miss-rate curve is NOT monotone below two stressors, and mix_c0 and mix_c1 have the LONGEST median execution times in the campaign (7.33 ms against 6.05) because the governor drops the clock under light load. (9) Dependency ranges measured at one version each except ruff, measured clean at both 0.16.9 and 0.17.5. (10) No cold-clone pip install was executed, so the ranges and the console entry point are unverified against a real install.
